G0900.def:
βαθύνω 
(βαθύς), [in LXX for עמד: Psa.91 (92):5, Jer.29 (49):8 30(49)30 * ;] 
to deepen: Luc 6:48.†

G0901.def:
βαθύς (genitive -έως, vernac., Lk, l.with; Bl., §8, 5), -εῖα, -ύ, 
[in LXX chiefly for עמק ;] 
deep; Jean 4:11; metaphorically, ὄρθρου βαθέως (see supr.), early dawn, Luc 24:1; ὕπνος, Actes 20:9; τὰ β. τοῦ Σατανᾶ, Apocalypse 2:24.†

G0902.def:
βαΐον, ου, τό
(also βὰϊον, another form of βὰϊς, from the Egyptian), [in LXX: 1Ma.13:51 * ;] (frequently in Egyptian π., see MM, Exp., x) 
a palm-branch: Jean 12:13 (DB, i, 314).†

G0903.def:
Βαλαάμ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בִּלְעָם), as in LXX (FlJ has ὁ βάλαμος); 
Balaam (Num.22-24): 2 Pierre 2:15, Ju 11, Apocalypse 2:14.†

G0904.def:
Βαλάκ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בָּלָק), 
Balak; (Nombres 22:2): Apocalypse 2:14.†

G0905.def:
βαλλάντιον (Rec. βαλά-), -ου, ὁ, 
[in LXX: Job 14:17 (צְרוֹר), Proverbes 1:14 (כִּיס), Tob.1:14 8:2, Sir.18:33 א 2 * ;] 
a purse: Luc 10:4 12:33 22:35, 36.†

G0906G.def:
βάλλω, 
[in LXX for נפל, שׂום, ידד, etc. ;] 
prop., of a weapon or missile; then generally, of things and persons, lit. and metaphorically, to throw, cast, put, place: with accusative, before εἰς, Matthieu 4:18, and frequently ἐπί, Matthieu 10:34; κάτω, Matthieu 4:6; ἔξω, Matthieu 5:13; ἀπό, Matthieu 5:29; ἐκ, Marc 12:44; δρέπανον, Apocalypse 14:19; μάχαιραν, Matthieu 10:34; κλῆρον, Matthieu 27:35; of fluids, to pour: Matthieu 9:17, Jean 13:5; pass., to be laid, to lie ill: Matthieu 9:2; ἐβλήθη (timeless aor., M, Pr., 134), Jean 15:6; intrans., to rush (Bl., §53, 1): Actes 27:14. Metaphorical, β. εἰς τ. καρδίαν, Jean 13:2 (cf. usage in π., without idea of violence; also of liquids; MM, Exp., x; see also Cremer, 120, 657; cf. ἀμφι-, ἀνα-, ἀντι-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐμ-, παρ-εμ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, μετα-, παρα-, περι-, προ-, συμ-, ὑπερ-, ὑπο-βάλλω).

G0906H.def:
βάλλω, 
[in LXX for נפל, שׂום, ידד, etc. ;] 
prop., of a weapon or missile; then generally, of things and persons, lit. and metaphorically, to throw, cast, put, place: with accusative, before εἰς, Matthieu 4:18, and frequently ἐπί, Matthieu 10:34; κάτω, Matthieu 4:6; ἔξω, Matthieu 5:13; ἀπό, Matthieu 5:29; ἐκ, Marc 12:44; δρέπανον, Apocalypse 14:19; μάχαιραν, Matthieu 10:34; κλῆρον, Matthieu 27:35; of fluids, to pour: Matthieu 9:17, Jean 13:5; pass., to be laid, to lie ill: Matthieu 9:2; ἐβλήθη (timeless aor., M, Pr., 134), Jean 15:6; intrans., to rush (Bl., §53, 1): Actes 27:14. Metaphorical, β. εἰς τ. καρδίαν, Jean 13:2 (cf. usage in π., without idea of violence; also of liquids; MM, Exp., x; see also Cremer, 120, 657; cf. ἀμφι-, ἀνα-, ἀντι-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐμ-, παρ-εμ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, μετα-, παρα-, περι-, προ-, συμ-, ὑπερ-, ὑπο-βάλλω).

G0906I.def:
βάλλω, 
[in LXX for נפל, שׂום, ידד, etc. ;] 
prop., of a weapon or missile; then generally, of things and persons, lit. and metaphorically, to throw, cast, put, place: with accusative, before εἰς, Matthieu 4:18, and frequently ἐπί, Matthieu 10:34; κάτω, Matthieu 4:6; ἔξω, Matthieu 5:13; ἀπό, Matthieu 5:29; ἐκ, Marc 12:44; δρέπανον, Apocalypse 14:19; μάχαιραν, Matthieu 10:34; κλῆρον, Matthieu 27:35; of fluids, to pour: Matthieu 9:17, Jean 13:5; pass., to be laid, to lie ill: Matthieu 9:2; ἐβλήθη (timeless aor., M, Pr., 134), Jean 15:6; intrans., to rush (Bl., §53, 1): Actes 27:14. Metaphorical, β. εἰς τ. καρδίαν, Jean 13:2 (cf. usage in π., without idea of violence; also of liquids; MM, Exp., x; see also Cremer, 120, 657; cf. ἀμφι-, ἀνα-, ἀντι-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐμ-, παρ-εμ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, μετα-, παρα-, περι-, προ-, συμ-, ὑπερ-, ὑπο-βάλλω).

G0906J.def:
βάλλω, 
[in LXX for נפל, שׂום, ידד, etc. ;] 
prop., of a weapon or missile; then generally, of things and persons, lit. and metaphorically, to throw, cast, put, place: with accusative, before εἰς, Matthieu 4:18, and frequently ἐπί, Matthieu 10:34; κάτω, Matthieu 4:6; ἔξω, Matthieu 5:13; ἀπό, Matthieu 5:29; ἐκ, Marc 12:44; δρέπανον, Apocalypse 14:19; μάχαιραν, Matthieu 10:34; κλῆρον, Matthieu 27:35; of fluids, to pour: Matthieu 9:17, Jean 13:5; pass., to be laid, to lie ill: Matthieu 9:2; ἐβλήθη (timeless aor., M, Pr., 134), Jean 15:6; intrans., to rush (Bl., §53, 1): Actes 27:14. Metaphorical, β. εἰς τ. καρδίαν, Jean 13:2 (cf. usage in π., without idea of violence; also of liquids; MM, Exp., x; see also Cremer, 120, 657; cf. ἀμφι-, ἀνα-, ἀντι-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐμ-, παρ-εμ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, μετα-, παρα-, περι-, προ-, συμ-, ὑπερ-, ὑπο-βάλλω).

G0909.def:
βαπτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (βαπτίζω), prop., the act of which βάπτισμα is the result; 
__1. a dipping, washing, lustration: Marc 7:4; of Jewish ceremonial. Hébreux 9:10; in Hébreux 6:2, βαπτισμῶν διδαχήν (-ῆς), "the pl. and the peculiar form seem to be used to include Christian baptism with other lustral rites" (Westc, in l.). 
__2. baptism: FlJ, Ant., 18, 5, 2 (of John's baptism), and some Fathers (see Soph., see word). Not so in NT, unless ἐν τ. βαπτισμῷ, in the act of baptism, Colossiens 2:12, be read with Tr. (Rec., WH, R, -ματι).
†

G0910.def:
βαπτιστής, -ου, ὁ (βαπτίζω), 
a baptizer: of John the Baptist, Matthieu 3:1 11:11, 12 14:2, 8 16:14 17:13, Marc 6:25 8:28, Luc 7:20, 33 9:19.†

G0911.def:
βάπτω, 
[in LXX chiefly for טבל ;] 
__(a) to dip: Luc 16:24, Jean 13:26 (ἐμβ-, L); 
__(b) to dip in dye, to dye: Apocalypse 19:13 (Rec.; ῥεραντισμένον, WH; περιρεραμμένον, T; ῥεραμμένον, Swete, in l., which see).
†

G0912.def:
Βαραββᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (Aram. בַּר־אַבָּא, lit., son of a father, i.e. accusative to Jerome, filius magistri), 
Barabbas: Matthieu 27:16, 17 20, 21, 26, Marc 15:7, 11 15, Luc 23:18, Jean 18:40. (In Matthieu 27:16, some MSS. read Ἰησοῦν Β.; see WH, App., 19f.).†

G0913.def:
Βαράκ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בָּרָק), 
Barak (Juges 4:6): Hébreux 11:32.†

G0914.def:
Βαραχίας, -ου, ὁ (Heb. בֶּרֶכְיָה), 
Barachiah: Matthieu 23:35, see: Ζαχαρίας.†

G0915.def:
βάρβαρος, -ον (prob. onomatop., descriptive of unintelligible sounds), 
[in LXX: Ps 113 (114):1 (לעז), Eze.21:31 (36) (בּער), 2Ma.2:21 4:25 10:4, 3Ma.3:24 * ;] 
barbarous, barbarian, strange to Greek language and culture (and also, after the Persian war, with the added sense of brutal, rude): Actes 28:2, 4 Romains 1:14, 1 Corinthiens 14:11, Colossiens 3:11 (see Lft., in l., and Notes, 249).†

G0916.def:
βαρέω, -ῶ (later form of βαρύνω, which see), 
[in LXX: Exode 7:14 (כָּבֵד), 2Ma.13:9 * ;] 
to depress, weigh down. In NT, in pass. only: Matthieu 26:43, Luc 9:32 21:34, 2 Corinthiens 1:8 5:4, 1 Timothée 5:16.†

G0917.def:
βαρέως, adv. 
(βαρύς), [in LXX: β. φέρειν, Genèse 31:35 (חרה בעיני); β. ἀκούειν, Ésaïe 6:10 (כּבד hi.)* ;] 
heavily, with difficulty: Matthieu 13:15, Actes 28:27" (LXX) .†

G0918.def:
Βαρθολομαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Aram. בַּר־תָּלְמַי, son of Tolmai), 
Bartholomew, the Apostle (see: Ναθαναήλ): Matthieu 10:3, Marc 3:18, Luc 6:14, Actes 1:13.†

G0919.def:
Βαρι-ησοῦς, -οῦ, ὁ (Aram. בַּר־יֵשׁוּעַ, son of Joshua), 
Bar-Jesus: Actes 13:6 (see: Ἐλύμας).†

G0920.def:
Βαριωνᾶς, Βαριωνᾶ, -ᾶ, ὁ (Aram. בַּר־יוֹנָה, son of Jonah), 
Bar-Jonah, a surname of Peter: Matthieu 16:17.†

G0921G.def:
Βαρναβᾶς, -α, ὁ (Aram. בַּר, son, as prefix to another word interpreted in Actes 4:36, τῆς παρακλήσεως, perh. נְבוּאָה, wh., however, should be rendered by προφητεία as in II Esther 6:14, LXX. Deiss., BS, 309f., thinks Β. may be a variant of the name Βαρνεβοῦς, son of Nebo, found in a Syrian Inscr., altered with a view to disguising its origin; see also Milligan, NTD, iii; Dalman, Gr., 142), 
Barnabas: Actes 4:36 9:27 11:22, 30 12:25 13-15, 1 Corinthiens 9:6, Galates 2:1, 9 13, Colossiens 4:10.†

G0923G.def:
Βαρσαββᾶς (Rec. -αβᾶς), -ᾶ (Aram., son of Sabba), 
Barsabbas: 
__1. the surname of one Joseph: Actes 1:23. 
__2. The surname of one Judas: Actes 15:22.
†

G0923H.def:
Βαρσαββᾶς (Rec. -αβᾶς), -ᾶ (Aram., son of Sabba), 
Barsabbas: 
__1. the surname of one Joseph: Actes 1:23. 
__2. The surname of one Judas: Actes 15:22.
†

G0924.def:
Βαρτίμαιος, -ου, ὁ (-μαῖος, T; perh. Aram. בַּר־טִמְאַי, see DB, iv, p. 762), 
Bartimæus: Marc 10:46.†

G0926.def:
βαρύς, -εῖα, ύ, 
[in LXX chiefly for כָּבֵד ;] 
heavy: Matthieu 23:4. Metaphorical, burdensome: ἐντολή, 1 Jean 5:3; severe (perh. impressive): ἐπιστολή, 2 Corinthiens 10:10; weighty: τὰ βαρύτερα τ. νόμου, Matthieu 23:23; αἰτιώματα, Actes 25:7; violent, cruel (EV, grievous): λύκος, Actes 20:29.†

G0927.def:
βαρύτιμος, -ον 
(βαρύς, τιμή), 
of great value, very costly: Matthieu 26:7 (T, πολυτίμου) .†

G0928G.def:
βασανίζω 
(βάσανος), [in LXX: 1 Rois 5:3, Sir.4:17, and frequently in Wi, II, 4Mac ;] 
__1. prop., to rub on the touchstone, put to the test. 
__2. to examine by torture, hence, generally, to torture, torment, distress: Matthieu 8:6, 29 14:24, Marc 5:7 6:48, Luc 8:28, 2 Pierre 2:8, Apocalypse 9:5 11:10 12:2 14:10 20:10.
†

G0928H.def:
βασανίζω 
(βάσανος), [in LXX: 1 Rois 5:3, Sir.4:17, and frequently in Wi, II, 4Mac ;] 
__1. prop., to rub on the touchstone, put to the test. 
__2. to examine by torture, hence, generally, to torture, torment, distress: Matthieu 8:6, 29 14:24, Marc 5:7 6:48, Luc 8:28, 2 Pierre 2:8, Apocalypse 9:5 11:10 12:2 14:10 20:10.
†

G0929.def:
βασανισμός, -οῦ, ὁ 
(βασανίζω), [in LXX: 4Ma.9:6 11:2 * ;] 
torture, torment: Apocalypse 9:5 14:11 18:7, 10, 15.†

G0930.def:
βασανιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (βασανίζω), 
prop., a torturer; used of a gaoler, Matthieu 18:34.†

G0931.def:
βάσανος, -ου, ὁ (of Oriental origin), 
[in LXX chiefly for כְּלִמָּה ,אָשָׁם, and frequently in 4Mac ;] 
__1. prop., touchstone, a dark stone used in testing metals. 
__2. examination by torture. 
__3. torment, torture: Matthieu 4:24, Luc 15:23, 28.
†

G0932.def:
βασιλεία, -ας, ἡ 
(βασιλεύω), [in LXX chiefly for מַמְלָכָה ,מַלְכוּת ;] 
__1. prop. abstract, sovereignty, royal power, dominion: Luc 1:33 22:29, Jean 18:36, Actes 1:6, Hébreux 1:8, 1 Corinthiens 15:24; λαβεῖν β., Luc 19:12, 15 Apocalypse 17:12; δοῦναι τὴν, ib. 17; ἔχειν β., ib. 18; ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τ. (εἰς τὴν) β., Matthieu 16:28, Luc 23:42; β. τ. θεοῦ, Apocalypse 12:10. 
__2. By meton., concrete (MM, Exp., x), 
__(a) a kingdom, the territory or people over whom the king rules (Esther 5:3, al.): Matthieu 4:8 12:25, 26 24:7, Marc 3:24 6:23, Luc 4:5, Hébreux 11:33, al.; 
__(b) the royal majesty (cf. our phrase His Majesty), the king himself (τ. σπέρμα τῆς β., 4Ki.11:1). 
__3. In LXX (Wis.6:5, Tob.13:1, al.), Targ. and NT, of the Messianic rule and kingdom, ἡ β. τ. θεοῦ, τ. οὐρανῶν (Heb. מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, Aram. מַלְכוּתָא דִשׁמַיָּא; see Dalman, Words, 91-147; Cremer, 132, 658), the kingdom of God (on the equivalence of the two phrases, see Dalman, op. cit., 93, 218f.); τ. θεοῦ, Matthieu 6:33 12:28, al.; τ. οὐρανῶν, Matthieu 3:2 4:17, al.; τ. Χριστοῦ (מַלִכוּת דִמְשִׁיחא, Targ. Jon. on Ésaïe 53:10), Éphésiens 5:5; τ. κυρίου, 2 Pierre 1:11, Apocalypse 11:15; τ. Δαυείδ, Marc 11:10; absol., ἡ β., Matthieu 4:23, Jacques 2:5, al. The kingdom is regarded as present: Matthieu 11:12, Luc 17:21, Romains 14:17, al.; as that which is to be consummated in the future, Matthieu 6:10, Marc 9:1, Jean 3:5, 2 Pierre 1:11, al. Noteworthy phrases are: ζητεῖν τὴν β., Matthieu 6:33; δέχεσθαι, Marc 10:15; κλρονομεῖν, Matthieu 25:34; διδόναι, Lk 12:32; παραλαμβάνειν, Hébreux 12:28; αὐτῶν (τοιούτων) εστὶν ἡ β., Matthieu 5:3, 10 19:14, Marc 10:14, Luc 18:16; διὰ τὴν β., Matthieu 19:12; ἕνεκεν τῆς β., Luc 18:29; εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, κηρύσσειν, διαγγέλλειν τὴν β., Luc 4:43 9:2, 60; ἤγγικεν ἡ β., Matthieu 3:2, Marc 1:15; κλεῖς τῆς β., Matthieu 16:10; κλείειν τὴν β., Matthieu 23:14; υἱοὶ τῆς β., Matthieu 8:12 13:38 (cf. Cremer, 132, 658).

G0933.def:
βασίλειον, -ου, τό 
(βασίλειος, which see), [in LXX for הֵיכָל ( Nahum 2:6, Daniel 6:18*), מַמְלָכָה ( 3Ki.3:1 14:8, 4Ki.15:19*), etc. ;] 
__1. a capital city. 
__2. Freq. in pl., τὰ β., a palace: Luc 7:25.
†

G0934.def:
βασίλειος, -ον (also -α, -ον; βασιλεύς), 
[in LXX; Exode 19:6, Deutéronome 3:10 (מַמְלָכָה), Exode 23:22, Wis.18:15, 3Ma.3:28, 4Ma.3:8 * ;] 
royal: 1 Pierre 2:9 (LXX) (see Hort, in l.).†
royal, regal, kingly;, metaphorically possessed of high prerogatives and distinction, 1Pet. 2:9;

G0935.def:
βασιλεύς, -έως, ὁ, 
[in LXX chiefly for מֶלֶךְ ;] 
a king: Matthieu 1:6 2:1; used by courtesy of Herod the Tetrarch, Matthieu 14:9; of the Roman Emperor, as frequently in κοινή (Deiss., LAE, p. 367), 1 Pierre 2:13, 17; of the Christ, in the phrase ὁ β. τ. Ἰουδαίων, Matthieu 2:2, al.; τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, Marc 15:32, Jean 1:50 12:13; of God, Matthieu 5:35, 1 Timothée 1:17, Apocalypse 15:3; β. βασιλέων, Apocalypse 17:14 19:16; β. τ. βασιλευόντων, 1 Timothée 6:15 (on the associations of the word to Jewish Hellenists, see Cl. Rev., i, 7).†

G0936.def:
βασιλεύω, (βασιλεύς), 
[in LXX for מלךְ, its parts and derivatives, exc. 4Ki.15:5 (ישׁב) ;] 
to be king, to reign, rule: 1 Timothée 6:15; with genitive (cl.), Matthieu 2:22; before ἐπί, with accusative (= Heb. מלךְ על; Bl., §36, 8), Luc 1:33 19:14, 27 Romains 5:14; ἐπὶ τ. γῆς, on earth, Apocalypse 5:10; of God, Apocalypse 11:15, 17 19:6; of Christ, Luc 1:33, 1 Corinthiens 15:25, Apocalypse 11:15; of Christians, Apocalypse 5:10 20:4 (constative aor., M, Pr., 130), ib. 6 22:5. Metaphorical, Christians, Romains 5:17, 1 Corinthiens 4:8; θάνατος, Romains 5:14, 17; ἁμαρτία, Romains 5:21 6:12. Ingressive aor. (M, Pr., 109), to begin to reign: 1 Corinthiens 4:8, Apocalypse 11:17 19:6 (Cremer, 137).†

G0937.def:
βασιλικός, -ή, -όν (βασιλεύς), 
[in LXX for מֶלֶךְ and its cognates ;] 
royal, belonging to a king: χώρα, Act 12:20; ἐσθής, Actes 12:21; νόμος β., a supreme law, "a law which governs other laws and so has a specially regal character" (Hort), or because made by a king (LAE, p. 3673), Jacques 2:8; τις, one in the service of a king, a courtier, Jean 4:46, 49 (WH, mg., βασιλίσκος).†

G0938G.def:
βασίλισσα, -ης, ἡ (in Attic, βασιλεία, βασιλίς), 
[in LXX chiefly for מַלְכָּה ;] 
a queen: Matthieu 12:42, Luc 11:31, Actes 8:27, Apocalypse 18:7.†

G0938H.def:
βασίλισσα, -ης, ἡ (in Attic, βασιλεία, βασιλίς), 
[in LXX chiefly for מַלְכָּה ;] 
a queen: Matthieu 12:42, Luc 11:31, Actes 8:27, Apocalypse 18:7.†

G0939.def:
βάσις, ־εως, ἡ 
(βαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for אֶדֶן ;] 
__1. a step (Æsch., al.). 
__2. Hence, a foot (Plat.; Wis.13:18): Actes 3:7.
†

G0940.def:
βασκαίνω, 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 28:54, 56 (רעע), Sir.14:6, 8*.] 
__1. to slander (Dem.). 
__2. to blight by the evil eye, to fascinate, bewitch: Galates 3:1.
†

G0941.def:
βαστάζω, 
[in LXX: Juges 16:30 (נטה), Ruth 2:16, 2 Rois 23:5, 4Ki.18:14 and Job 21:3 (נשׂא), Sir.6:25, Da TH Bel 36 * ;] 
__1. to take up with the hands, to lift: λίθους, Jean 10:31. 
__2. to bear, to carry, as a burden, and metaphorically, to endure; Matthieu 3:11 20:12, Marc 14:13, Luc 7:14 10:7 11:27 14:27 22:10, Jean 16:12 19:17, Actes 3:2 9:15 15:1 21:35, Romains 11:18 15:1, Galates 5:10 6:2, 5 17, Apocalypse 2:2, 3 17:7. 
__3. In late writers (MM, Exp., ii, iii, x), 
__(a) to take away; Matthieu 8:17 (Ésaïe 53:4, Heb.); 
__(b) to carry off, steal: Jean 12:6 20:15.
†

G0942.def:
βάτος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ, 
[in LXX (always masc, as in Attic): Exode 3:2-4, Deutéronome 33:16 (סְנֶה), Job 31:40 (בָּאְשָׁה)* ;] 
a bramble-bush: Luc 6:44, Actes 7:30, 35; ἐπὶ τοῦ (τῆς) β., in the place concerning the bush: Marc 12:26, Luc 20:37.†

G0943.def:
βάτος, -ου, ὁ (Heb. בַּת), 
[in LXX (also βαίθ, βάδος): II Esther 7:22 * ;] 
bath, a Jewish liquid measure, = μετρητής (which see), or about 8 3/4 gals.: Luc 16:6.†

G0944.def:
βάτραχος, -ου, ὁ, 
[in LXX: Ex 8, Psa.77 (78):45 104 (105):30 (צְכַרִדֵּעַ), Wis.19:10 * ;] 
a frog: Apocalypse 16:13.†

G0945.def:
βατταλογέω, -ῶ (Rec. βαττολ-, D, βλαττ- = βατταρίζω, prob. onomatop.; see MM, see word; DCG, ii, 499b, 790a); 
to stammer, repeat idly: Matthieu 6:7 (Cremer, 765).†

G0946.def:
βδέλυγμα, -τος, τό 
(βδελύσσω), [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁקֶץ ,תּוֹעֵבָה ;] 
an abomination, a detestable thing: Luc 16:15, Apocalypse 17:4, 5 21:27; τὸ β. τ. ἐρημώσεως (Dan LXX 12:11, cf . 1Ma.1:54; DB, i, 12f.; DCG, i, 6f.), Marc 13:14, Matthieu 24:15 (Cremer, 138).†

G0947.def:
βδελυκτός, ή, -όν 
(βδελύσσω), [in LXX: Proverbes 17:15 (תּוֹעֵבָה), Sir.41:5, 2Ma.1:27 * ;] 
abominable, detestable: Tite 1:16 (Cremer, 137).†

G0948.def:
βδελύσσω, βδελύσσομαι 
(βδέω, to stink), [in LXX chiefly for שׁקץ ,תּעב ;] 
in cl., mid. only (Attic, -ττομαι); to make foul; pass., Apocalypse 21:8; mid., to turn away in disgust from, to detest: Romains 2:22 (Cremer, 137).†

G0949.def:
βέβαιος, -ον (also -α, -ον; βαίνω), 
[in LXX: Esther 3:13, Wis.7:23, 3Ma.5:31 7:7, 4Ma.17:4 * ;] 
firm, secure: ἄγκυρα, Hébreux 6:19; metaphorically, sure (esp. "in the sense of legally guaranteed security," Deiss., BS, 109; cf . two foll. words): ἐπαγγελία, Romains 4:16; ἐλπίς, 2 Corinthiens 1:6; λόγος, Hébreux 2:2; παρρησία, Hébreux 3:6; ἀρχή (τ. ὑποστάσεως), Hébreux 3:14; διαθήκη, Hébreux 9:17; κλῆσις κ. ἐκλογή, 2 Pierre 1:10; comp. (-ότερος), προφητικὸς λόγος, 2 Pierre 1:19.†

G0950.def:
βεβαιόω, -ῶ 
(βέβαιος), [in LXX: Ps 40 (41)12 (נצב hi.), 118 (119)28 (קוּם pi.), 3Ma.5:42 * ;] 
to confirm, establish, secure, of things (cl.): λόγον, Mk 16:[20]; ἐπαγγελίας, Romains 15:8; of persons (DCG, ii, 605): 1 Corinthiens 1:8, 2 Corinthiens 1:21. Pass., 1 Corinthiens 1:6, Colossiens 2:7, Hébreux 2:3 13:9 (as an Attic legal term, to guarantee the validity of a purchase, establish or confirm a title; see next word, Cremer, 139; cf. δια-β.).†

G0951.def:
βεβαίωσις, -εως, ἡ 
(βεβαιόω, which see), [in LXX: Lévitique 25:23 (צְמִיתֻת), Wis.6:19 * ;] 
confirmation: τ. εὐαγγελίου, Philippiens 1:7; εἰς β., Hébreux 6:16, a phrase frequently in π. of guarantee in a business transaction (Deiss., BS, 104ff.; Cremer, 140).†

G0952.def:
βέβηλος, -ον 
(βαίνω, whence βηλός, a threshold), [in LXX chiefly for חֹל ;] 
__1. permitted to be trodden, accessible (see DCG, ii, 422b); hence, 
__2. (opposite to ἱερός) unhallowed, profane: of things, 1 Timothée 4:7 6:20, 2 Timothée 2:16; of men, 1 Timothée 1:9, Hébreux 12:16 (cf. κοινός; Cremer, 140).
†

G0953.def:
βεβηλόω, -ῶ 
(βέβηλος), [in LXX chiefly for חלל ;] 
to profane: τ. σάββατον, Matthieu 12:5; τ. ἱερόν, Actes 24:6 (Cremer, 141).† 
SYN.: κοινόω, which see

G0954.def:
Βεελζεβούλ (WH, App., 159, Rec., βεελζεβούλ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בַּעַל, lord, and the Talmudic זִבּוּל, from זֶבֶל, dung (Dalman, Gr., 137.n), or perh. זִבֻל, habitation, but, see DB, iv, 409f.; DCG, i, 181). The AV, RV, Beelzebub, comes through Vg. from 4Ki.1:2, בַּעַל זִבוּב, lord of flies (LXX, βάαλ μυῖα, Sm., βεελζεβούβ), 
Beelzebul, Beelzebub, a name of Satan: Matthieu 10:25 12:24, 27 Marc 3:22, Luc 11:15, 18 19.†

G0955.def:
Βελίαλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בְּלִיַּעַל, worthlessness, but see DB, i, 268), 
Belial, a name of Satan: 2 Corinthiens 6:15, Rec. See next word.†
Βελιάρ, ὁ, indecl. (another form of previous word, "due to harsh Syriac pronunciation," or else Heb. בֵּל יַעַר, lord of the forest), 
Beliar, a name of Satan: 2 Corinthiens 6:15 (see DB, i, 269).†

G0956.def:
βέλος, -εος, τό 
(βάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for חֵץ ;] 
a missile, a dart: Éphésiens 6:16.†

G0957.def:
βελτίων, -ον (genitive -ονος), comp. of ἀγαθός, 
[in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;] 
neut. as adv., better, very well: 2 Timothée 1:18 (also Actes 10:28 D). On elative use in these passages, see M, Pr., 78, 236.†

G0958.def:
Βενιαμίν, (Rec. -μίν), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בֶּנְיָמִין), 
Benjamin: Actes 13:21, Romains 11:1, Philippiens 3:5, Apocalypse 7:8.†

G0959.def:
Βερνίκη (elsewhere Βερενίκη), Macedonian form of Φερενίκη, cf. Veronica, Victoria), -ης, ἡ, 
Bernice, Berenice, dau. of Herod Agrippa I: Actes 25:13, 23 26:3o.†

G0960.def:
Βέροια, -ας, ἡ, 
Berœa, a city of Macedonia: Actes 17:10, 13.†

G0963.def:
Βηθανία, -ας (also -ιά, indecl., Luc 19:29 and in B*, Marc 11:1), ἡ, (Heb. בֵּית עֲנִיָּה, house of affliction, accusative to Jerome, or perh., house of dates, cf. Bethphage), 
Bethany; 
__1. a village fifteen furlongs from Jerusalem, the modern El Azerîyeh: Matthieu 21:17 26:6, Marc 8:22 (WH, mg.) 11:1, 11, 12 14:3 Luc 19:29 24:50, Jean 11:1, 18 12:1. 
__2. A place on E. bank of Jordan: Jean 1:28 (R, mg., Βηθαβαρά, which see).
†

G0964.def:
Βηθεσδά, ἡ, indecl. (deriv. uncertain, see Westc. on Jean 5:2, and DB, i, 279), 
Bethesda, a pool in Jerusalem: Jean 5:2, Rec. (Βηθζαθά, WH, Βηθσαϊδά, WH, mg.).†

G0965.def:
Βηθλέεμ, ἡ, indecl. (Heb. בֵּית לֶחֶם, house of bread), 
Bethlehem, a town 6 m. S. of Jerusalem: Matthieu 2:1, 5 6, 8, 16, Luc 2:4, 15 Jean 7:42.†

G0966.def:
Βηθσαιδά (Rec. -σαϊδά), and -δάν (Mt, Mk, ll. with), ἡ, indecl. (Syr., house of fish), 
Bethsaida, a town on NE. shore of the Sea of Galilee: Luc 9:10. It is generally supposed that a second B. on the W. shore is referred to in Matthieu 11:21, Marc 6:45 8:22, Luc 10:13, Jean 1:45 12:21 (DB, i, 282f.; but see Swete on Marc 6:45). 
__2. 2. Βηθζαθά, ἡ, indecl. (perh. Aram. בֵּית זַיְתָה, house of olives) Jean 5:2..†

G0967.def:
Βηθφαγή (L, -γῆ), ἡ, indecl. (Aram. בֵּית־פַּגֵּי, house of unripe figs; Dalman, Gr., 191), 
Bethphage: Matthieu 21:1, Marc 11:1, Luc 19:29.†

G0968.def:
βῆμα, -τος, τό 
(βαίνω), [in LXX: Deutéronome 2:5 (מִדְרָךְ), Néhémie 8:4 (מִגְדָּל), I Esther 9:42, Sir.19:30 45:9, 2Ma.13:26 * ;] 
__1. a step, stride, pace: Actes 7:5. 
__2. a raised place, a platform reached by steps, originally that in the Pnyx at Athens from which orations were made; frequently of the tribune or tribunal of a Roman magistrate or ruler: Matthieu 27:19, Jean 19:13, Actes 12:21, 18:12, 16, 17 25:6, 10, 17; β. τοῦ θεοῦ, Romains 14:10; τ. Χριστοῦ, 2 Corinthiens 5:10.
†

G0969.def:
βήρυλλος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ, 
[in LXX: Tob.13:17 (-ύλλιον in Exode 28:20, שֹׁהַם * ;]) 
beryl, a jewel of sea-green colour: Apocalypse 21:20.†

G0970.def:
βία, -ας, ἡ, 
[in LXX for פֶּרֶךְ, etc. ;] 
strength, force, violence: Actes 5:26 21:35 24:7 27:41.†

G0971.def:
βιάζω (βία), and depon. -ομαι, 
[in LXX for פּרץ, פּצר, etc. ;] 
to force, constrain, rare in active (poet, and late prose), but found in cl. in pass., and so perh. βιάζεται, suffereth violence, Matthieu 11:12, EV (but see infr.), whether 
__(a) in good sense, of disciples (Thayer, al.), or 
__(b) in bad sense, of the enemies of the kingdom (Meyer, in l.; Dalman, Words, 139ff.; Cremer, 141ff.). Mid., advanceth violently, Mt, l.with (Deiss., BS., 258; Banks, see ref. in DCG, ii, 803f.); before εἰς, to press violently, or force one's way into, Luc 16:16 (see ICC, in l., and in Mt, l.with; cf. παραβιάζομαι and see MM, see word).
†

G0972.def:
βίαιος, -α, -ον 
(βία), [in LXX for אָנַשׁ, עַז, צַר, etc. ;] 
violent: Actes 2:2.†

G0973.def:
βιαστής, -οῦ, ὁ (βιάζω), late form of βιατάς; 
__1. strong, forceful. 
__2. violent (Philo): Matthieu 11:12 (see: βιάζω).
†

G0974.def:
βιβλαρίδιον, -ου, τό (diminutive of βιβλάριον, diminutive of βίβλος), 
a little book: Apocalypse 10:2, 8 (WH, βιβλιόν, T2, 7 βιβλιδάριον) 9, 10. Not hitherto found elsewhere.†

G0975.def:
βιβλίον, -ου, τό (diminutive of βίβλος, which see), 
[in LXX also in the alternat. form βυβ-, chiefly for סֶפֶר and the most frequently of the cognate forms ;] 
__1. a paper, letter, written document: β. ἀποστασίου, bill of divorce, Matthieu 19:7, Marc 10:4. 
__2. a book, a roll: Luc 4:17, 20 Jean 20:30 21:25, Galates 3:10, 2 Timothée 4:13, Hébreux 9:19 10:7, Apocalypse 1:11 5:1-9 6:14 10:8 20:12 22:7-19; β. τ. ζωῆς, Apocalypse 13:8 17:8 20:12 21:27.
†

G0976.def:
βίβλος, -ου, ἡ (variant form of βύβλος, the Egyptian papyrus, paper made from its fibrous coat), 
[in LXX for סֶפֶר, the form βύβ- being sometimes used ;] 
a book, a roll, used much less frequently than βιβλίον, and with a "connotation of sacredness and veneration" (MM, Exp., x), Matthieu 1:1 Marc 12:26, Luc 3:4 20:42 Actes 1:20 7:42 19:19; β. τ. ζωῆς, Philippiens 4:3, Apocalypse 3:5 20:15.†

G0977.def:
βιβρώσκω, poët, and late prose, 
[in LXX for אכל ;] 
to eat: Jean 6:13.†

G0978.def:
Βιθυνία, -ַας, 
Bithynia, a province in Asia Minor: Actes 16:7, 1 Pierre 1:1.†

G0979.def:
βίος, -ου, ὁ, 
[in LXX chiefly for יָמִים ;] 
__1. period or course of life, life: Luc 8:14, 1 Timothée 2:2, 2 Timothée 2:4, 1 Jean 2:16. 
__2. living, livelihood, means (in Proverbes 31:14 for לֶחֶם; see DCG, ii, 39a): Marc 12:44, Luc 8:43 15:12, 30 21:4, 1 Jean 3:17.† 
SYN.: ζωή, is life intensive, "vita quâ, vivimus," the vital principle; βίος, life extensive, "vita quam vivimus," (1) the period of life, (2) the means by which it is sustained. Hence, in cl., ζ., being confined to the physical life common to men and animals, is the inferior word (cf. zoology, biography). In NT, ζωή is elevated into the ethical and spiritual sphere (cf. Tr., Syn., §xxvii).

G0980.def:
βιόω, -ῶ 
(βίος), [in LXX: Proverbes 7:2 9:6 (חיה), Job 29:18, Wis.4:4 א 1, 12:23, Sir.40:28, 4Ma.5:22 17:18 * ;] 
to spend life, to live: τ. χρόνον βιῶσαι (cl., more frequently 2 aor., -ναι), 1 Pierre 4:2 (cf. Jb, l.with).† 
SYN.: ζάω (which see).

G0981.def:
βίωσις, -εως, ἡ 
(βιόω), [in LXX: Si prol. 12 * ;] 
manner of life: Actes 26:4.†

G0982.def:
βιωτικός, -ή, -όν 
(βιός), 
pertaining to life, hence, worldly (Field, Notes, 171): Luc 21:34, 1 Corinthiens 6:3, 4.†

G0984.def:
βλάπτω, 
[in LXX: Proverbes 25:20, Tob.12:2, Wis.10:8 18:2, 2Ma.12:22, 4Ma.9:7 * ;] 
to hurt, injure: with accusative, Mrk.16:[18], Luc 4:35.†

G0985.def:
βλαστάνω, 
[in LXX for צמח, etc. ;] 
__1. to sprout: Matthieu 13:26, Marc 4:27, Hébreux 9:4. 
__2. In late Gk., causal, to make to grow, produce: with accusative, Jacques 5:18.
†

G0986.def:
Βλάστος, -ου, ὁ, 
Blastus, chamberlain of Agrippa: Actes 12:20.†

G0987.def:
βλασφημέω, -ῶ 
(βλάσφημος), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:4 (יכח hi.) ib. 6, 22 (גּדף pi.), Ésaïe 52:5 (נאץ hith.), Dan LXX 3:29 (96) (אמר שׁלח), Tob.1:18, Da TH Bel 9, 2Ma.2 * ;] 
__1. to speak lightly or profanely of sacred things (in cl., opp. of εὐφημέω), esp. to speak impiously of God, to blaspheme, speak blasphemously: absol., Matthieu 9:3 26:65, Marc 2:7, Jean 10:36, Actes 26:11, 1 Timothée 1:20, 2 Pierre 2:12; τ. θεόν, Actes 19:37, Apocalypse 16:11, 21; τὸ ὄνομα τ. θεοῦ, Apocalypse 13:6 16:9; δόξας, Ju 3, 2 Pierre 2:10; εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, Marc 3:29, Luc 12:10. 
__2. to revile, rail at, slander: absol., Luc 22:65, Actes 13:45 18:6, 1 Pierre 4:4; with accusative, Matthieu 27:39, Marc 3:28 15:29, Luc 23:39, Tite 3:2, Jacques 2:7, Ju 10. Pass.: Romains 2:24 3:8 14:16, 1 Corinthiens 10:30, 1 Timothée 6:1, Tite 2:5, 2 Pierre 2:2 (Cremer, 570).
†

G0988.def:
βλασφημία, -ας, ἡ 
(βλάσφημος), [in LXX: Eze.35:12 (נֶאָצָה), Da TH 3:29 (96) (שׁלה), Tob.1:18, 1Ma.2:6, 2Ma.8:4 10:35 15:24 * ;] 
__(a) railing slander: Matthieu 12:31 15:19, Marc 3:28 7:22, Éphésiens 4:31, Colossiens 3:8, 1 Timothée 6:4, Ju 9, Apocalypse 2:9 
__(b) spec., impious speech against God, blasphemy: Matthieu 26:65, Marc 14:64, Luc 5:21, Jean 10:33, Apocalypse 13:5; ὄνομα βλασφημίας, Apocalypse 13:1 17:3; with genitive obj. Matthieu 12:31; πρὸς τ. θεόν, Apocalypse 13:6 (Cremer, 570; DB, i, 305; DCG ii, 423).†

G0989.def:
βλάσφημος, -ον 
(βλασ-, of uncertain deriv., see Thayer, Boisacq; + φήμη, speech), [in LXX: Ésaïe 66:3 (מְבָרֵךְ אָוֶן), Wis.1:6, Sir.3:16, 2Ma.9:28 10:4, 36 * ;] 
__(a) evil-speaking, slanderous, blasphemous: Actes 6:11, 2 Timothée 3:2, 2 Pierre 2:11 (cf. Ju 9); 
__(b) as subst. a blasphemer: 1 Timothée 1:13 (Cremer, 570).
†

G0990.def:
βλέμμα, -τος, τό 
(βλέπω), 
a look, a glance: βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ, 2 Pierre 2:8, sight and hearing, a sense not found for β. in Gk. lit., but perh. recognized in the vernacular (ICC, in l.)†

G0992.def:
βλητέος, -α, -ον (gerundive of βάλλω), 
(that which) one must put: Luc 5:38.†

G0993.def:
Βοανηργές, indecl. (on the derivation, see Dalman, Gr., 144; Words, 42; Swete, Mk., l.with; DCG, i, 216), 
Boanerges: Marc 3:17.†

G0994.def:
βοάω, -ῶ 
(βοή), [in LXX chiefly for זעק, צעק, קרא ;] 
__1. absol., to cry, call out: Matthieu 3:3, 27:46, Marc 1:3 15:34, Luc 3:4 9:38 18:38, Jean 1:23, Actes 8:7 17:6 25:24, Galates 4:27. 
__2. C. dative, to call on for help (Heb. זעק על, Osée 7:14, al.), Luc 18:7.† 
SYN.: καλέω, to call, invite, summon; κράζω, to cry, harshly or inarticulately, as animals; κραυγάζω, intensive of κράζω. βοάω expresses emotion, whether joy, fear, etc.

G0995.def:
βοή, -ῆς, ἡ, 
[in LXX for זְעָקָה, etc. ;] 
a cry: Jacques 5:4.†

G0996.def:
βοήθεια, -ας, ἡ (see: βοηθέω), 
[in LXX for עֵזֶר, etc. ;] 
help: Hébreux 4:16; pl., helps, "frapping," a technical nautical term (MM, Exp., x; DB, ext., 367): Actes 27:17.†

G0997.def:
βοηθέω, -ῶ 
(βοή + θέω, to run), [in LXX chiefly for עזר ;] 
to come to aid, to help, succour: absol., Actes 21:28; with dative, Matthieu 15:25, Marc 9:22, 24 Actes 16:9, 2 Corinthiens 6:2" (LXX), Hébreux 2:18, Apocalypse 12:16.†

G0998.def:
βοηθός, -ον (see: βοηθέω), 
[in LXX chiefly for עזר ;] 
__1. (poët. -όος), hasting to the war-cry (Hom.). 
__2. helping, auxiliary; as subst. (Hdt.), a helper: Hébreux 13:6 (LXX).
†

G0999.def:
βόθυνος, -ου, ὁ (= βόθρος, more frequently in cl.), 
[in LXX chiefly for פַּחַת ;] 
a pit: Matthieu 12:11 15:14, Luc 6:39 (cf. DB, iii, 885; DCG, ii, 367).†
